reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) describes DFT methods for elastic constants, electronic structure, and analytical transport models assuming quenched disorder, but none provides specific prior evidence for MD simulation of anharmonic vibrations, DFT calculation of oxygen defect states on carrier mobility, or the coupling of MD and DFT to predict conductivity in this alloy. The key premises about the mechanism and predictive accuracy are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: MD can simulate anharmonic lattice vibrations and dynamic disorder in HfNbTaTiZr with 1 wt.% oxygen
DFT can calculate electronic structure including oxygen-induced defect states and their effect on carrier mobility
Coupling MD and DFT captures temperature-dependent carrier concentration and mobility missed by perfect-crystal models
Oxygen-induced defect scattering and anharmonic effects cause a marked conductivity downturn at 0–200 K due to carrier localization
The proposed MD+DFT approach will predict room-temperature conductivity within 7% of experiment
